title: Plugin activation retention policy scratchpad
content:
Context and goals:

This is a personal scratchpad to explore a lightweight, privacy-conscious retention policy for 'plugin activation' artifacts used by sandboxed extensions and local adapters. The motivation: we need to keep enough activation context to support fast re-activation, safe debugging, and post-mortem traces, while minimizing user-data retention surface and storage cost.

High-level requirements (non-exhaustive):
- Fast reactivation: if a plugin is called again within short window, avoid cold start (warmup hooks, cached handshake).
- Explainability/debugging: keep minimal trace to reconstruct activation sequence for a customer incident.
- Privacy-first: do not persist sensitive prompt payloads longer than necessary; respect consent flags and tenant-level retention overrides.
- Configurable by tenant and by runtime: hosted vs private deployments need different defaults.
- Low cost: small, bounded per-activation footprint; eviction TTLs and size caps.

Invariants and constraints:
- Activation records must be auditable but never contain PII or full prompt text by default. We store digests and controlled metadata.
- Activation token keys are rotated and bounded; long-term keys live in KMS-managed vaults only in Private deployments.
- Retention rules cascade: global default -> tenant override -> per-plugin opt-in/opt-out.

Activation record proto (text sketch, minimal fields):
- activation_id: uuid
- tenant_id: short id
- plugin_id: short id
- caller_context_hash: sha256 of normalized caller metadata (no raw prompt)
- timestamp_start, timestamp_end
- result_code: enum (ok, user_abort, plugin_error, infra_error)
- warmup_hint: boolean (true if we expect imminent re-use)
- resource_profile: small tag (cpu_light, gpu_heavy, io_bound)
- telemetry_link: pointer to telemetry span id (not raw logs)
- retention_tier: enum (ephemeral, short, medium, long)
- audit_digest: signed digest of activation inputs stored in vault if tenant requires longer retention

Notes on caller_context_hash:
- Hashing must be done after deterministic normalization: remove timestamps, strip free-text parts, canonicalize headers. This enables grouping without storing raw user content.
- Provide a reversible audit path only when tenant opt-in and with KMS access; otherwise only the hash exists.

Retention tiers and suggested defaults (hosted API vs private):
- ephemeral: 1 hour (default for most activations on hosted plans)
- short: 24 hours (when warmup_hint=true or immediate retry patterns)
- medium: 30 days (tenant-declared diagnostic mode, must be consented)
- long: 365 days (enterprise legal/archival, only in Private with explicit contract)

Eviction and size control heuristics:
- Per-tenant daily cap: X MB/day across activation records (configurable). When cap exceeded, evict oldest ephemeral entries first.
- Per-plugin max records: small bounded queue (e.g., 200 recent activations) for in-memory warm caches.
- Global archive queue: periodic rollup that compacts telemetry links and digests; raw payloads are never kept unless audit_digest is present and tenant allows.

API shape (sketch) for activation lifecycle:
1) POST /v1/plugins/{id}/activate -> returns activation_id, warmup_token_expiry
   payload includes: plugin_version, minimal caller fingerprint, opt_in_retention (enum)
2) PATCH /v1/activations/{activation_id}/complete -> includes result_code, telemetry_span_id, resource_profile
3) GET /v1/activations/{activation_id}?view=meta|audit -> meta returns metadata fields; audit returns signed digest reference (requires tenant KMS auth)
4) DELETE /v1/activations/{activation_id} -> tenant-initiated immediate purge (honor legal hold exceptions)

Flow diagram (ASCII):
[plugin-call] -> [activation-service: create record (ephemeral)] -> [runtime-router] -> [plugin-sandbox exec] -> [complete patch to activation] -> [short cache for warmup] -> (if warmup_hint) keep in in-memory LRU for 30s -> async compactor moves to short-tier store or deletes

Telemetry and observability considerations:
- Activation records should link to existing span ids rather than duplicate logs. The activation record stores telemetry_link:trace_id:span_id.
- Sampled payload logging: only if tenant enabled; otherwise sample by hash buckets to keep debugging coverage without storing raw inputs.
- Metrics to emit: activation_rate, reactivation_ratio(within_1min), average_activation_duration, activation_error_distribution, retention_overage_events.

Privacy and compliance notes:
- Default must be privacy-preserving: store no free-form prompt or attachments.
- Audit path (full payload storage) requires tenant opt-in and explicit KMS-protected envelope. Access audited with SIEM hooks.
- Data subject delete: deleting tenant data should cascade and remove all activation records and compacted digests unless flagged for legal hold.

Configuration knobs we should surface in Console and API:
- default_retention_tier (global + per-tenant override)
- per-plugin retention_override (must be opt-in)
- daily_storage_cap_mb and policy when cap exceeded (evict_oldest|stop_accepting_warmups|notify)
- telemetry_sampling_rate and hash_buckets_for_sampling

Open questions / TODOs:
- Exact size of activation record on wire. Need a micro-benchmark: (expected ~300-600 bytes for meta only).
- How to represent multi-tenant plugin proxies where a single activation spans multiple sub-tenants? Need canonicalization rules for tenant_id.
- Should warmup_hint be a scored float instead of boolean to allow smarter eviction? (pros: fidelity; cons: complexity & risk of misuse)
- Integrations with existing log retention (Console) and with Optimize pipeline for eviction suggestions.
- UX: surface a retention-preview UI that shows estimated storage and costs for a tenant if they bump to medium/long tiers.

Small checklist for next steps (personal):
- [ ] run quick size benchmark on activation stub with current proto sketch (samir to help with bench harness)
- [ ] draft lightweight API contract + Swagger for activation endpoints (convert to repo PR)
- [ ] prototype in-memory warm cache with LRU + reactivation counter
- [ ] write short RFC: externalize retention tiers and legal hold semantics

Notes-to-self: keep this doc intentionally conservative on defaults for hosted. Lean on tenant opt-in for anything >24h. Communicate costs clearly in Console when tenant requests longer retention.

End of scratchpad.
